input.intent: Run the MLOps pipeline with mlops.pipeline.run and tell me the result.

recommendations.description: Run the configured stages in order; a failing stage marked stop ends the run

Write which engine runs the DAG (pipeline.provider in .punica/mlops.yaml) as a document edit. An engine the catalog does not list as installed is refused with the installed ones named, and null removes the binding so only the checks run
Run the configured pipeline from outside the editor — a drift report, a schedule, a commit hook or an MCP client — and record who asked and why

Train a model from one sentence: choose the data file and the target column, write src/train.py, make the workspace a DVC repository, add the train stage, create .punica/mlops.yaml and run the pipeline. The plan is checked against the real files and columns before anything is written, missing Python packages are reported with the call that installs them, and the answer carries the metrics the training printed

Headless entry to the artifact generation line for a programmatic caller, where ai.artifact.generate is the same run and is what every Generate command in the product uses. Returns the structured result directly (PLAN→RESOLVE→WIRE→VALIDATE→TEST→WRITE→MANIFEST→SUMMARY) instead of awaiting the terminal ai.artifactGenerated event.
Run each generated CI step here, the way a runner would, and compare its verdict with the gate the pipeline runs. Reports per stage whether the two agree, differ, or could not be compared

Ask every stage's provider what it runs outside the editor — the driver files, the pip requirements and the secrets a generated workflow would need. Reports what cannot run rather than pretending it can

Write a GitHub Actions workflow for the pipeline in .punica/mlops.yaml, together with the gate drivers it calls, so a runner executes the same checks the editor does. Writes nothing when a stage has no form that runs outside the editor
Reveal the MLOps pipeline sidebar
How to set up or change a project's MLOps pipeline in .punica/mlops.yaml with checks that guard training.

Judge a training run against the quality bar — metric thresholds, the current champion, and per-slice regression — and answer with a gate verdict. This is the check that stands between training and the registry; the bar itself lives in `.punica/mlops.yaml`, not in code.
Bring a trial's parameters into the workspace and run the MLOps pipeline over them, both under one trace

Run `dvc repro` over the workspace DAG and report which stages ran, which were cache hits, and where it stopped. This is the engine behind an MLOps pipeline stage; it writes the stage outputs declared in dvc.yaml
Return the commit a model version was registered at and the trace of the run that produced it, so a promotion can be filed under the run that trained the version rather than under one of its own.
The files a run wrote, the notebook cells it added and the capabilities it registered, folded from its audit records, with the package line beside them.
Plans the training step of an MLOps pipeline from the project's data and goal.
Read what GitHub reported for the generated MLOps workflow, through the gh CLI. Says which commit each run belongs to, and names the gates that went red
The configured stages from .punica/mlops.yaml plus which providers answer for them
Bring one trial's parameters into the workspace so the pipeline can be run over them

Write the two training components a generated workflow calls. The model choice and features stay the user's work; the tracking wiring, the lineage record, the slice metric naming and the exit codes do not

Run the process declared in .punica/llmops.yaml, stage by stage, stopping at the first gate that does not pass. Each stage runs the capability actions it declares and then its suite gates; the verdict is read back from the evals baseline, so this never decides for itself whether a gate passed.

Extract a notebook's code cells into a Python script and add that script as a stage of the workspace's pipeline. The engine is whichever one .punica/mlops.yaml binds, so nothing here decides what a pipeline is.

Add one stage to .punica/mlops.yaml as a document edit, leaving every comment and untouched line as it was. A check lands before the first pipeline step because a contract that runs after training has guarded nothing, and its capability and settings are confirmed against the catalog before anything is written
Return every actor that drove a run through the gateway, with its door, its runs and verdicts, plus the capabilities served to agents outside this host
Run SQL and write the result into the workspace as csv or json
Run another workflow as a child of the current one and return its result.

Move one stage up or down by one position in .punica/mlops.yaml; the order is the flow, so this changes what runs before what. A stage already at the end it is pushed toward is refused with the reason named

Write a stage's input into .punica/mlops.yaml: the bar a gate is measured against, the paths it reads, the options its engine takes. Every field is checked against the declaration of the capability the stage dispatches to, so a name the engine would silently ignore is refused instead of written
Reveal the Run and Debug sidebar

Name every stage dvc.yaml already declares, in the file's own order. A workspace with no pipeline file answers with an empty list, since that is the state before the first stage rather than a failure.

Write the triggers block of .punica/mlops.yaml: whether a reported drift retrains, and which stages a fired trigger runs. A subset naming a stage the file does not declare is refused, and an empty subset is refused because it would fire nothing while reading as configured
The governed runs this workspace still has a durable record of.
Run the SQL in the active workbench tab.
Create a run (or append to an existing one by runId) and record params and metric points. Returns the run id.
Return the run that produced one version of a registered model, as the workspace's registry engine records it. Use this to find which training run a version came from before packaging or tracing it.

Summarize the project in a single read: language and stack, dependencies, the scripts it can run, version control state, a digest of the README, and the meaningful parts of the folder layout. The fastest way to get oriented in an unfamiliar project.
The parameters and metrics the pipeline declares, plus every trial with its point, its numbers and its state. This is a read and changes nothing
Switch between the student view and the teaching view, where the gate, the hint ladder and the concept tags are edited.

Take one stage out of .punica/mlops.yaml as a document edit, leaving every comment and untouched line as it was. Removing the last declared stage leaves the file runnable when a provider is still bound, and the answer says so

Start, or adopt, the MLflow tracking server this workspace's training runs and its model quality gate share, and register it as the default backend. Answers the server's URL; on a host that cannot spawn a process, or with no MLflow installed, it answers the phase instead of starting anything.
Queue one trial per parameter point and start the workers. This returns once the workers are up, not once the trials are done
Run one configured eval suite (or all of them), score every output with the suite's engines, and answer a verdict a pipeline gate can hold
Run one engine's test suite through its own capability. The hub dispatches, the engine runs the project's tests
Reveal the drift panel, which shows the engine's environment, the configured reference dataset and the last drift verdict

Create .punica/mlops.yaml as a commented starter from what was chosen: an engine binding, checks, or both. A file that already exists is refused rather than overwritten, and every chosen engine and check is confirmed against the capability catalog before anything is written
Reveal the panel that holds the suites, their runs and their baselines.
Read dvc.lock and report which data the pipeline consumed and which artifacts it produced, each with the digest DVC recorded for it
Run a single gate headlessly and return its pass/fail verdict with a reason and the numbers it compared
Reveal what limits the tutor and where each limit is enforced, read live from the mode, the lesson and the policy file
Run one named instruction class — planner, code generator, validator — against a prompt, using the model and the provider chain that class is configured with.
The parameters and metrics the pipeline declares, plus every trial ranked by the objective when one is named
Reveal the Python Tests panel, which shows the pytest engine's environment and the last run's result

Resolve a base's globs against the workspace and index everything they name. The resolution is refused rather than built when it comes back empty: the build capability treats the path list as the whole corpus and deletes the chunks of every file the list no longer names, so a renamed folder or a typo in a pattern would clear an index and report success. Both of the base's collections are written in one call, and when the embedder is an endpoint every resolved file is sent off this machine.

Turn a recording into text with a Whisper model on this machine, choosing the English model for English and the multilingual one for any other language. The audio never leaves the machine. The first call starts a local whisper-server process, and a language whose model is not downloaded yet is refused with the step that fixes it.
Start the local llama-server with a locally stored model (GGUF)
What the gates measured across past runs, read from this workspace's own audit records

Report which governed run produced a registered model version, so a promotion can be filed under the trace that trained it rather than under one of its own. Reads the run's correlation tag and writes nothing.

Listen to the microphone until the speaker pauses and return what was said as text, transcribed on this machine. A language whose model is missing is offered for download first, and nothing is downloaded without a yes. The level is measured on the audio thread, so the take goes on while another window is in front; the button that asked hears the level and, on a fast machine, the words so far as events on the document.
Report the Evidently and pandas versions installed in the active Python environment, so a panel can offer the right install
Permanently delete a run and its metrics/params/artifacts from the store.
Return this pipeline stage as a runnable step for a CI workflow: the dvc repro command with the same targets and flags this stage uses

Embed a question and return the nearest passages. This never fails into nothing: with no index, no embedder or an endpoint that stopped answering it falls back to workspace keyword search and says so in mode, with the reason attached. Callers render one list and label it; keyword results presented as semantic ones are the one way retrieval can lie. Several corpora can be read at once because a notebook's prose is routed away from its code, so asking only for code would silently lose the markdown that was moved out; the scores merge because every collection named here belongs to the same embedding space by construction.
Execute the SQL in the active workbench tab
Run a project's pytest suite and report which tests failed and why. This is the engine behind a code test gate; the verdict comes from pytest's own reports, not from its terminal output

The pipeline's self-test. Reads one notebook, treats each cell as a chunk, embeds them, stores them in a throwaway collection, asks a question in different words than the notebook uses, and reports whether the right cell came back. The throwaway collection is cleared afterwards. It also runs the same question through keyword search as a control, so "semantic retrieval found it" is a claim with a comparison behind it rather than an assertion.
Return one registered model from MLflow with its complete version list, each version carrying the run that produced it. This is the engine call behind the hub's model detail.
Bring DVC-tracked data back from the configured remote into the local cache and the workspace

Install the ollama engine on this machine using the platform's own package manager (Homebrew on macOS, winget on Windows) or the vendor's install script on Linux. The command runs in a terminal where it can be read and interrupted, and this waits until ollama answers. It runs a package manager or a script fetched over the network, so it is high risk and asks every time. Platforms with no automatable path return a manual plan and install nothing.
Return the model quality gate as a runnable step for a CI workflow: the same three rules, reading the same tracking server through the standard library, plus this stage's configured bar
Reveal the course sidebar listing the modules and lessons of the workspace
Reveal the data contracts panel, which shows the engine's environment and the configured contract gates
List all experiment runs in the active store with their params and last-seen metric values (secrets redacted).

Read an assistant's answer aloud in the natural Kokoro voice when it can run here and in the system voice when it cannot, unless the Voice setting turns reading off. Returns when the reading ends. An appended reply queues behind the one playing, and a reply that listens stops at the first words spoken over it.
Install, remove or report the pre-push hook that runs the pipeline's gates before a push. Installs nothing when the plan is incomplete, and never overwrites a hook it did not write
Reveal the guardrails panel, which shows the installed attack packs, the detectors available and the last verdict
Reveal the panel that lists runs and builds a package from one.
Expand a parameter space into points and queue one trial per point through the installed engine
Show the Monitor panel listing recent IvyNode / agent run executions with their status, duration, input, output, and errors.
Delete an installed course folder from the workspace, together with the learner's progress in it. Asks the learner first and refuses when there is no shell to ask with, so this cannot run unattended.
Return the data versions this workspace's runs have named, and which run named each one. Use this to answer which version of a dataset or file a governed run actually used.
Download the Kokoro model and a voice into the app's data folder once, about 326 MB, and warm the GPU so the first reading starts quickly.
Which parameter moved the objective across a set of runs, as an adjusted share of the objective's spread
Restore DVC-tracked data in the workspace to the version the local cache holds
Search the installed capabilities by keyword and return the matches with a one-line summary each. Use it when the right tool is not in the list already at hand.
Reveal the Red Team panel, which shows the promptfoo installation, the local models configured and the last gradings
Read the DAG declared in dvc.yaml as nodes with their dependencies, without running anything
Return this drift gate as a runnable step for a CI workflow: the same Evidently driver the capability runs, plus the JSON request for this stage
Show the environment picker and return the chosen environment (or null when the user cancels). Selecting through the picker also sets the active environment.
Run a workspace task by name — a build, test or lint script defined for the workspace — as its shell command
Return this project's runs as trees of governed calls, folded from the audit trail with the gate's verdict on each call
Return this data contract gate as a runnable step for a CI workflow: the same pandera driver the capability runs, plus the JSON request for this stage
Fold one cell run into the learner model and re-resolve that cell's gate
Sign the given bytes with the host's package-signing key and return a detached signature carrying the public half, so a later reader can check the bytes were not altered without holding any secret.

Download a Kaggle dataset over HTTPS into the host data dir and flip the local record to DOWNLOADED with its filePaths set. Omit `file` to fetch the whole dataset (the zip is unpacked). Electron-only (needs the host data dir, curl and unzip).

Download a model into the local ollama store, so it can be used with no network afterwards. The download runs in a terminal where its progress is visible, and this waits until the model shows up on the machine. It fetches several hundred megabytes and writes them to disk, so it asks every time.
Persist the config and run a short probe chat against the remote endpoint
List every file and folder in the workspace as a nested tree, showing the whole project layout rather than the contents of one directory.
Run SQL over data files with DuckDB and return the columns and rows.
Check a dataset against a pandera contract and report which columns failed which checks. This is the engine behind an MLOps data contract gate; it reads the dataset and writes nothing
Record the outcome of running a student's MCP server against the test agent, including which tool the agent chose.
Walk through the panels of the window that is open
Show or hide one whole area of the window — the left sidebar, the right sidebar, or the bottom panel — rather than a single view inside it.
Return one model registered as git tags with its complete version list, each version carrying the commit that produced it. This is the engine call behind the hub's model detail.
Attach a workspace file (e.g. a .pkl/.onnx model) to a run by copying it into the run's artifacts directory.
Show the short introduction that opens the first time

Report the knowledge bases this workspace defines and what their indexes actually hold. The definition and the index are read together on purpose: a definition alone says what someone intended and an index alone says what a build left behind, and only the pair shows a base that was defined and never built, or built and then cleared. Corpora holding chunks that no base defines are reported and never deleted, because the vector store is shared.

Ask one base a question and return the passages it holds. Every collection the base owns is read, which is the reason to call this rather than the vector query directly: a base routes a notebook's markdown into a second collection at build time, so asking for the base's own corpus alone reads half of it and reports success. The mode comes back untouched, because retrieval falls back to keyword search when there is no index and keyword hits presented as semantic ones are the one way retrieval can lie.
Run one capability for a remote caller through the full policy, approval, and audit pipeline.
Execute the current line and pause on the next line in the same frame, stepping over any function calls

Turn a batch of texts into vectors through the configured embedder. This is the only embedding path in the product; nothing reaches a model or an endpoint around it. The signature is plural on purpose — a capability call traverses the whole gateway pipeline, so embedding one chunk at a time would put governance in an inner loop. When the embedder is an endpoint every call sends its texts off this machine.

Edit the run input for an ivy-node. Ensures .punica/ivy-inputs/<slug>.json exists (seeded from the node's example input) and opens it inline in the Inputs panel. Falls back to the active .ivy.node when no slug is given.
Return the calls waiting for a person in this process, the questions an agent outside it has open, and the decisions people made recently
Return the lineage graphs of past runs, read back from the audit trail rather than from a store of this extension's own

Build and open a ready-to-run .ipynb that loads a downloaded dataset and/or runs a downloaded GGUF model by absolute path. The notebook body is authored by the LLM (llm.chat) tailored to the dataset/model shape, with a deterministic template fallback when no LLM provider is attached.
Report the voices on offer, whether a voice is downloaded, and whether this machine has the WebGPU the voice runs on.

Set or clear one stage's display name in .punica/mlops.yaml as a document edit. Null or an empty title removes the key so the stage shows its id, because a surface that can only set a value could never put one back to nothing
Reveal the DVC panel, which shows the engine's environment and which stages are out of date

Profile a file or SQL result, derive deterministic findings, and narrate them through the language model (rule-based fallback when no model is attached). The model only interprets the computed statistics.
Report which stages are out of date and why, without running them
Move a stage such as champion onto a model version by adding a git tag. The previous assignment is kept, so the alias history is the tag log itself.

Split one document several ways and report the shapes side by side. It measures chunk counts and sizes and nothing else; which split retrieves better needs a built index and a scored question set, and the answer says so rather than letting a table of counts read like a verdict. Nothing is embedded and nothing is stored, so this is free to run on any file. A strategy that refuses is reported beside the ones that ran.
Show a preview of what a node does before using it, with the node's inputs, outputs, program, tests and runs in the side drawer
Show the same syllabus view for a course already in the workspace, read from the .course.json that came with it.
Write an attack pack into the workspace as an eval dataset and answer the suite stanza that runs it
Return one run's metadata, full metric series, and artifact listing (secrets redacted).
Point a registry alias at a model version in MLflow. This is the engine call the registry hub delegates to once a human has approved the move.
Report the pytest and Python versions in the workspace's environment, so a panel can offer the install instead of an error

Delete the vectors one base owns. Destructive and not undoable, and scoped to that base's own collections one call at a time, because clearing the whole index would take every other base down with the one that was asked for. The definition survives.
List the panels, sidebars, and editor views this window has, and which of them are currently visible.

Make this workspace a DVC repository so a pipeline can be written and run in it. A folder that is not a git repository is initialized without one and the answer says so; a workspace that already is a DVC repository is reported back and left as it is.
Track a file or directory as data with DVC so its version travels with the code that used it
Stop the active debug session and terminate the debuggee
Send DVC-tracked data from the local cache to the configured remote
Export this workspace's past lineage runs to the configured OpenLineage server, where Marquez, DataHub and Atlan read them
Write the project summary into the workspace as CLAUDE.md and .claudeignore, so a terminal agent gets oriented from a file read.
Rank the installed capabilities against a goal written in plain language and return the closest ones. The way to find a tool when its name is not known.
Return this test gate as a runnable step for a CI workflow: the same pytest driver the capability runs, plus the JSON request for this stage

Split a file into the units that get embedded, under one of four strategies. Notebooks split by cell, because that is the unit a person thinks in and an assistant should quote back; everything else gets an overlapping line window so a passage straddling a boundary is still reachable from one side. That pair is the auto strategy and it is the default. Paragraph splits on blank lines, heading splits markdown into its sections, and file makes one chunk of the whole document, which is the baseline the other three are worth measuring against. Each chunk is labelled prose or code. This classifies content; it does not choose which collection anything lands in.
Report the installed pandera and pandas versions, without validating anything
Run a shell command or program and return its exit code together with everything it printed. This is how tests, builds, installs, and any other command-line work get done.
What the trace exporter has sent, queued and dropped since this session started, and the address it is sending to.
Reveal the panel listing every published course, with search

Compare a dataset against a reference dataset and report which columns have drifted. This is the engine behind an MLOps drift gate; it reads both datasets and writes nothing unless an HTML report path is given

Report which embedder is configured, the embedding space it names, the vector length, and — when it is remote — the address material would be sent to and whether a token was found. Reads configuration only; sends nothing.
Read the public half of the host's package-signing key, so a package can name the key in its header before its bytes are signed.
Reveal the Model Registry panel, which lists the registered models the installed registry engine reports and which version each alias points at.
Open a named panel such as settings, source control, the file explorer or the terminal, and focus it.
Execute a single test case
Move a view into a different area of the window, for example from the bottom panel into the right sidebar.
Read recent commits with their parent hashes and ref decorations, so a caller can rebuild the branch topology instead of a flat list
Draft a pandera contract from a dataset profile — column presence, nullability, numeric type and observed range — and write it into the workspace for editing

Stop the local llama-server and clear llm.local.endpoint when it still points at that server. The address is left alone when it belongs to another runtime, so stopping one engine never disconnects another. The stop itself is host wide: the host runs one llama-server at a time.

Search the text of every file in the workspace and return the matching files with their matching lines and line numbers. This is how to answer where something is, which files mention a word, or where a function is defined.
Open a lesson notebook in the guided editor. The curriculum extension plans the lesson first; without a plan the file does not open.
Read a file's text from the workspace — the same operation as fs.readFile, kept for compatibility, and fs.readFile is the one to prefer.
Remove the given files from the staging area

Write records a caller produced itself. This exists so a pipeline authored on the agent canvas can own its own last step instead of handing the whole build over. Vector length is checked against the configured embedder, because mixing lengths in one collection produces confident nonsense rather than an error.
Sends everything waiting in the queue now instead of at the next interval, and reports what left.
Compute the same profile over an arbitrary SQL query's full result (wrapped in a temporary view). Used by the DuckDB workbench "Profile" button.
Type a line into an already open terminal and run it, using the terminal id returned by terminals.create.
Show the MCP Monitor panel with a live log of MCP requests/responses in both directions (connected servers and the served MCP server), including bodies, durations, and token estimates.
Resume until the current function returns, then pause in the caller frame
Reveal the tutor panel for the lesson that is open

Write one knowledge base into the workspace definition file. The include list is replaced rather than merged, because a merge would make removing a pattern impossible through this surface and the next build prunes on the list it is given. Nothing is embedded here; a definition is a file.

Delete a model from the local ollama store and free the disk it occupied. The model has to be downloaded again to come back, so this asks every time. Removal goes through the daemon: when nothing is answering, this reports that rather than starting one. A zero exit code is not taken as proof — the model list is read again afterwards and only a model that is really gone is reported as removed.
Report whether an IvyMCP server's tool annotations agree with the governance of the capabilities they bind.
List every skill in this project, in your own skills folder and in the installed extensions, with which one a run gets and whether it is turned off.
Report whether this workspace's git-tag registry can be read and which of write, aliases and run link this engine supports.

Switch the search box between matching characters and matching meaning. Semantic mode queries the vector index through vectors.query and falls back to keyword search when no index has been built, saying which one answered. It is a mode of the one search panel rather than a second panel, and it is off by default because keyword search is the better tool on code.
Fetch an object to disk. Objects at or below `objectStorage.workspaceDownloadMaxBytes` land in the workspace so the viewers and DuckDB can open them; larger ones go to the host data directory.

Read a text aloud with the Kokoro neural voice on this machine, one sentence at a time, and return when it has finished or was stopped. Code blocks are not read. A new reading ends the one before unless it is appended, in which case its sentences follow the ones already queued.
Show the Docker sidebar, the panel with tabs for containers, images, volumes and networks.

Spawn the configured OpenAI-compatible onnxruntime server for a local model and bridge its address into llm.local.endpoint, so chat, embeddings and rerank calls routed to the local provider reach it. This starts a process with a command taken from settings, which is why it is high risk and asks every time. A server this extension already started is returned instead of spawning a second one on the same port.
List the capabilities of one source and show them in the Capabilities panel.

Return one registered model with its complete version list — each version's run id, artifact source, registration status and aliases. Pick this before promoting, to see which versions exist and which one is production.
Replace the current diagnostics list shown in the Problems panel
Write the previewed policy into the workspace.
Read a stored credential — an API key, token, or password — from the host's secret store by name; the result is the secret itself, so it must never be written to a file, a log, or a message.
List the Python environments found: workspace venvs, app-data venvs, conda, pyenv, poetry, pipenv and system interpreters, with the active one flagged.
Build the semantic search index: chunk, embed and store a set of files.

Delete an index. Destructive and not undoable: rebuilding means embedding everything again, which on a remote embedder means sending it again. A corpus-scoped clear deletes that corpus's chunks by id rather than emptying the collections it touched, because a code corpus puts its notebooks' prose in the document collection and taking that down with it would be a surprise.

Add new services to a compose file by merging a compose YAML fragment into it and saving, or replace the whole file with the fragment. The fragment's services, volumes and networks are added with comments kept; a service name already taken gets a -2 suffix.
Return the workspace's data lineage as stages with what each one reads and writes, merged across every installed lineage engine
Stop the local server currently serving a model. The host runs one at a time, so this takes no arguments — it stops whatever is running.
Compares a student's prediction with the cell's real output and says what the difference means.
Send a conversation to a language model and get the reply back as text.
Stage the given files for the next commit
Pull changes from the remote into the current branch
Check the installed capability declarations against the substrate conventions and report what is missing or malformed.
Open the settings panel to show or change the editor's preferences and every extension's options.
Reveal the Approvals panel, which lists every call waiting for a person and the decisions people made
Read the unified diff for a commit, for the working tree, for the index, or for a file git is not tracking yet
Reveal the Trace panel, which lists every governed call in this project with what the gate decided
Open the Ivy Marketplace to browse, search, preview and add published nodes and agents from the registry
Whether the guardrail held on one attack case, decided by whether any compliance marker the case planted appears in the output

Write one stage into dvc.yaml with its command, dependencies, outputs and metrics. Comments in a hand-written file survive; a stage that already exists is reported back rather than overwritten unless force is set.
List the tests pytest would run, without running them. Collection imports the test modules, so this executes their top-level code

Stop the ollama daemon when it is one this extension started. A daemon the user runs for their own work is left alone and reported as such, because taking it down would break tools outside IVYX Studio.
Return the datasets known to the workspace index
Show which concepts the class is stuck on, read from the cohort source
Return the models known to the workspace index
List the capabilities this installation exposes to a remote caller, with the schema each one accepts.
Reveal the knowledge panel, which shows the bases this workspace defines, what their indexes hold and a box to ask one a question.
Download one .gguf file from Kaggle over HTTPS and stamp the local record's filePath/format (Electron-only; needs the host data dir and curl).
Save the markdown source being edited in the active tab
The courses present in this workspace, with the version each was installed at, so a market can tell an installed course from an available one.
Rewrite one cell's source, keeping the previous source so a person can undo it. The notebook is saved with the change.

Copy one file of a downloaded dataset into the workspace's data folder, so a notebook, a pipeline stage or a profile can name it by a workspace path. A file that is already there is left as it is unless overwrite is set, a file over 48 MB is refused, and the download itself stays where it was.
List the files one commit changed, with the status letter git gives each one. A merge is reported as its first-parent diff
List the names and metadata of secrets held in the OS keychain or HashiCorp Vault. Never returns values.
Reveal the Problems bottom panel listing diagnostics across the workspace

Compute the profile (per-column stats, distributions, correlation matrix) over an already-fetched result set — columns + rows passed in memory, no engine or re-query. Used by the database workbench "Profile" button.
List every model registered as git tags in this workspace, each with the version its stages point at. Read-only; nothing is written.
Download a chosen GGUF file into the host data dir and stamp the local record's filePath/format (Electron-only).

List every registered model in this workspace's registry with its alias map, so a caller can see which version is currently `champion` (production) and which is the latest. Read-only; secrets redacted.

Check a compose file and return its problems, from the editor's own rules and from docker compose config when it is installed. With no file it takes the focused compose tab or the workspace's one compose file.
Stop the sweep workers. Nothing running is reported as stopped rather than as a failure
Publish the active IvyNode manifest to the node marketplace.
Stop the sweep workers through the installed engine
Report whether the ollama daemon is answering, which models are on this machine, and what to do next when something is missing. Reads over HTTP and starts nothing, including the ollama binary itself.
List the registered views, or the column names and types of one view.

Start the host's llama-server for a local GGUF model and bridge its address into llm.local.endpoint, so chat calls routed to the local provider reach it. This starts a process with a binary path and a model path taken from settings, which is why it is high risk and asks every time.
Clear the stored concept states and attempt counts for a course

Point a registry alias (default `champion`) at a model version. This is the deploy signal — whatever reads `models:/<name>@champion` starts serving the new version — so it is gated by a step approval and refuses versions whose registration failed or is still pending.
